name: CC7 System Operations Relationship Set
description: Authoritative relationship graph for the CC7 vertical slice. Extends MAPSET-ACCESS-CORE and MAPSET-CC6 without repeating any edge already declared there. Edges are derived from the entity records, so convenience references and the graph cannot diverge.

traversal_notes: CC7 reuses several CC6 entities rather than duplicating them: EV-CONFIG-001, EV-VULN-001, and EV-ENDPOINT-002 carry CC7 edges alongside their CC6 edges, and FND-NETSEC-002 and REM-NETSEC-002 were extended to CC7.1 rather than cloned.
SOC2-CC7.1-001 predates this slice and its existing edges live in MAPSET-ACCESS-CORE; only its new relationships appear here.
The relationship vocabulary is identical across all three sets and the validator enforces that identically-named types carry identical definitions.

relationship_types.answers_question: Which evidence supports this control, and which controls does this evidence support?
Which questionnaire questions relate to this control?
What findings can this evidence reveal?
Which answers signal a potential gap?
What findings can indicate a gap in this control?
Which criteria are at risk from this finding?
How do we confirm the remediation actually landed?

mappings.rationale: Vulnerability Identification and Remediation contributes to CC7.2 in addition to its primary criterion CC7.1.
Vulnerability Identification and Remediation contributes to CC8.1 in addition to its primary criterion CC7.1.

Configuration Baseline Monitoring and Change Detection is DriftGuard's primary control articulation for CC7.1: Detect changes to system configuration that introduce new vulnerability or weaken an existing control, rather than discovering them at review time or during an examination.
Configuration Baseline Monitoring and Change Detection contributes to CC7.2 in addition to its primary criterion CC7.1.
Configuration Baseline Monitoring and Change Detection contributes to CC8.1 in addition to its primary criterion CC7.1.
Configuration Change History and Drift Record is primary evidence for Configuration Baseline Monitoring and Change Detection: Change history and drift record across the period.

Vulnerability Scan Result and Remediation Tracking is supporting evidence for Configuration Baseline Monitoring and Change Detection: Scan results corroborate whether configuration change introduced known vulnerability.
Network and Boundary Security Policy is where the standard Configuration Baseline Monitoring and Change Detection is measured against originates.
Vulnerability Management Policy is where the standard Configuration Baseline Monitoring and Change Detection is measured against originates.

Assesses Configuration Baseline Monitoring and Change Detection. Question intent: Establish whether change detection is continuous or review-based, and whether advisory monitoring exists separately from scheduled scanning.

Security Monitoring and Anomaly Analysis is DriftGuard's primary control articulation for CC7.2: Collect the telemetry needed to notice abnormal activity across in-scope components, and analyse what is noticed so that anomalies are assessed rather than merely recorded.
Security Monitoring and Anomaly Analysis contributes to CC7.1 in addition to its primary criterion CC7.2.
Security Monitoring and Anomaly Analysis contributes to CC7.3 in addition to its primary criterion CC7.2.
Security Log Source Coverage and Retention Configuration is primary evidence for Security Monitoring and Anomaly Analysis: Log source coverage, retention, and integrity configuration.
Security Alert and Event Evaluation Record is primary evidence for Security Monitoring and Anomaly Analysis: Alert population with analysis and disposition across the period.
Malicious Software Detection and Triage Record is supporting evidence for Security Monitoring and Anomaly Analysis: Endpoint detections are one anomaly source feeding the same analysis process.
Configuration Change History and Drift Record is supporting evidence for Security Monitoring and Anomaly Analysis: Evidences that monitoring configuration held through the period.
Logging and Security Monitoring Policy is where the standard Security Monitoring and Anomaly Analysis is measured against originates.

Assesses Security Monitoring and Anomaly Analysis. Question intent: Establish whether coverage is measured against the asset inventory rather than the logging platform's own source list, and whether retention reaches the examination period.
Assesses Security Monitoring and Anomaly Analysis. Question intent: Establish whether analysis is attributable, time-bounded, and recorded, which is what separates monitoring from collection.

Security Event Evaluation and Incident Declaration is DriftGuard's primary control articulation for CC7.3: Apply defined criteria to decide whether a security event has affected, or could affect, the entity's ability to meet its objectives, so that incident declaration is a judgement made against a standard rather than an improvised call.
Security Event Evaluation and Incident Declaration contributes to CC7.2 in addition to its primary criterion CC7.3.
Security Event Evaluation and Incident Declaration contributes to CC7.4 in addition to its primary criterion CC7.3.
Security Alert and Event Evaluation Record is primary evidence for Security Event Evaluation and Incident Declaration: Event population with evaluation outcome, including non-incident dispositions.
Security Incident Record is primary evidence for Security Event Evaluation and Incident Declaration: Declared incidents with the basis for declaration.
Incident Response Policy is where the standard Security Event Evaluation and Incident Declaration is measured against originates.

Assesses Security Event Evaluation and Incident Declaration. Question intent: Establish whether declaration is a judgement against a documented standard, and whether non-monitoring intake paths exist.

Incident Response Execution and Communication is DriftGuard's primary control articulation for CC7.4: Ensure that a declared incident is worked through a defined programme covering understanding, containment, remediation, and communication, and that the programme is exercised before it is needed.
Incident Response Execution and Communication contributes to CC7.3 in addition to its primary criterion CC7.4.
Incident Response Execution and Communication contributes to CC7.5 in addition to its primary criterion CC7.4.
Security Incident Record is primary evidence for Incident Response Execution and Communication: Incident records showing timeline, containment, participants, and communications.
Incident Response Plan Test Record is primary evidence for Incident Response Execution and Communication: Response plan test record and resulting improvement tracking.
Incident Response Policy is where the standard Incident Response Execution and Communication is measured against originates.
Assesses Incident Response Execution and Communication. Question intent: Establish whether the plan is tested within the period and whether the test produces outcomes rather than attendance.

Incident Recovery and Post-Incident Remediation is DriftGuard's primary control articulation for CC7.5: Restore affected systems to a known good state after an incident, and ensure the underlying cause is identified and addressed so the same failure does not recur.
Incident Recovery and Post-Incident Remediation contributes to CC7.4 in addition to its primary criterion CC7.5.
Incident Recovery and Post-Incident Remediation contributes to CC7.1 in addition to its primary criterion CC7.5.
Security Incident Record is primary evidence for Incident Recovery and Post-Incident Remediation: Recovery actions, post-incident review, and tracked remediation to closure.

Configuration Change History and Drift Record is supporting evidence for Incident Recovery and Post-Incident Remediation: Evidences that configuration was restored to and held at the intended baseline.

Vulnerability Scan Result and Remediation Tracking is supporting evidence for Incident Recovery and Post-Incident Remediation: Where the root cause was an unremediated vulnerability, closure is evidenced here.
Incident Response Policy is where the standard Incident Recovery and Post-Incident Remediation is measured against originates.

Assesses Incident Recovery and Post-Incident Remediation. Question intent: Establish whether review is triggered by a threshold and whether resulting actions are tracked somewhere closure can be demonstrated.
Failure of the existence check on Security Incident Record indicates Incident records do not evidence containment, communication, or timeline.
Failure of the sufficiency check on Security Incident Record indicates No post-incident review or review actions not tracked to closure.
Failure of the relevance check on Security Incident Record indicates No documented criteria for declaring a security event an incident.
Failure of the existence check on Incident Response Plan Test Record indicates Incident response plan not tested within the period.
Failure of the existence check on Security Log Source Coverage and Retention Configuration indicates Log source coverage or retention below what the period requires.
Failure of the relevance check on Security Log Source Coverage and Retention Configuration indicates Log integrity protection not addressed.
Failure of the existence check on Security Alert and Event Evaluation Record indicates Alerts generated without recorded analysis or escalation criteria.
Failure of the relevance check on Security Alert and Event Evaluation Record indicates No documented criteria for declaring a security event an incident.

Answer condition 'no named responder or analysis timeframe' signals Alerts generated without recorded analysis or escalation criteria.
Answer condition 'no written declaration criteria' signals No documented criteria for declaring a security event an incident.
Answer condition 'no exercise within the examination period' signals Incident response plan not tested within the period.
Answer condition 'no defined review trigger' signals No post-incident review or review actions not tracked to closure.

Log source coverage or retention below what the period requires places CC7.2 at risk; the edge exists so a gap can be reported even where the entity has named no control.

Log integrity protection not addressed places CC7.2 at risk; the edge exists so a gap can be reported even where the entity has named no control.
Protect log integrity or document the accepted position addresses Log integrity protection not addressed.
Alerts generated without recorded analysis or escalation criteria bears on the insufficient evidence assessment of Security Monitoring and Anomaly Analysis.
Alerts generated without recorded analysis or escalation criteria places CC7.2 at risk; the edge exists so a gap can be reported even where the entity has named no control.
Alerts generated without recorded analysis or escalation criteria places CC7.3 at risk; the edge exists so a gap can be reported even where the entity has named no control.

Assesses Vulnerability Identification and Remediation. Question intent: Establish whether scan scope derives from the authoritative asset inventory and whether overdue findings have a governed risk-acceptance path rather than simply remaining open.
Answer condition 'overdue findings have no documented risk acceptance path' signals Vulnerabilities unresolved beyond the organization's own remediation timeframe.

notes: MAP identifiers continue the single sequence begun in MAPSET-ACCESS-CORE and are never renumbered.
Edge rationales are composed from the source entity records; the substantive judgement lives in the record and is cited here.
MAP-0322 and MAP-0323 added during the CC7 quality gate to attach the pre-existing SOC2-CC7.1-001 to questionnaire coverage.
